characters.name: Kyle Broflovski
characters.description: Stan's closest friend. He and his parents are Jewish, but his younger brother, Ike, is actually from Canada. He appears to be the smartest of the original four — at least academically — but has a tendency to get sucked into the latest fads/problems/social issues sweeping South Park. Kyle is also known as the moral compass of the otherwise chaotic town — although he has a nasty temper to go along with it that especially comes out during his many clashes with his arch-nemesis Cartman. His role in Coon and Friends is The Human Kite. Academic Athlete: A young version. Kyle's favorite sport, in-series, is basketball; he is also seen participating in soccer, baseball, and football, all while demonstrating high scholastic intelligence (hiswimpy cousinKyle even calls him a "redneck jock stereotype" in one episode). Accidental Hero: In “Follow That Egg!”, Mrs. Garrison makes a deal with the governor of Colorado that she can get him a scientific study proving gay couples can’t raise children, said study being her students who are paired up and assigned to take care of eggs, with Stan and Kyle representing a gay couple. Despite her efforts to sabotage them (to the point of hiring a hitman to try and take out their egg), Stan and Kyle are able to get their egg safely to the press conference, and the governor declares that gay couples can get married. When Randy tells the boys he's proud of them, a confused Kyle asks, "What did we do?" Aesop Amnesia: Hits thishardafter COVID, particularly in "Streaming Wars" and "The War on Obesity". He repeatedly forgets all the times Cartman has put his life in danger even when he had nothing to gain and bends over backward to his whim only for him to be screwed over by Cartman yet again.

characters.name: KennyMcCormick
characters.description: An immortal, hedonistic, vulgar, but courageous and selfless boy that comes from a very poor family that often has to struggle to survive.He used to get killed offOnce per Episodeonly to come back to life later, but that's not the case anymore... usually, since the creators were getting tired of killing Kenny off in every episode and running out of original ways to kill him. He almost always speaks with a muffled voice, with various levels of intelligibility. His role in Coon and Friends is Mysterion. Alliterative Family: With his brother Kevin and sister Karen. His mother Carol's name is also pronounced with a hard "k" sound. All Men Are Perverts: One of the prominent young examples on the show. He's the most sexually knowledgeable of the boys and often fantasizes about the female body. Ambiguously Human: He has the habit of hiding almost his entire face and is the only character in the show to consistently die and be reborn again to the point wherea trope was even named after him.As of the Coon & Friends trilogy, it's generally accepted that Kenny is implied to be some sort ofEldritch Abominationlarva in human skin orisone due to him being able to do things humans aren't capable of, such as hisResurrective Immortality.

characters.name: Evil Parallel Universe
characters.description: Evil versions of the boys from a parallel universe. The Bad Guy Wins: Though they're defeated and sent back to their universe, Evil Stan and Evil Kyle succeed in bringing Evil Cartman back with them, thanks to mainline Cartman's ingenuity. Beard of Evil: The evil versions of the boys all sport goatees. The Bully: According to Evil Cartman, both Evil Stan and Evil Kyle are usually really mean to him for no reason. Later in the episode, the two of them endeavor to get their Cartman back, apparently only out of a desire to continue tormenting him. Dying Curse: As he's being sent back to his universe, Evil Cartman yells out his first and last "screw you guys!" directed at the boys. Downplayed since he's just being sent home via an apparently painful method.

characters.name: Panderverse
characters.description: Versions of the boys from a universe where everyone is a woman of color. Ambiguous Gender: They all appear to be biological women, but their universe doesn't appear to even have biological men in it, and not only do they constantly refer to each other in masculine terms but they aren't surprised when they encounter biological men by crossing universes. Ambiguously Gay: It's not clear if all four of them are lesbians or if it's just Kenny. Badass Arm-Fold: The quartet all assume tough girl poses, with Kenny and Cartman folding their arms as if to establish that these are strong independent women. Dawson Casting:Invoked. They're clearly too old to be elementary school students and possibly too old to even be high school students. Given the special is mocking Disney's casting choices, it's most likely a dig at how they cast 20-something actresses as protagonists who are canonically in their mid-late teens.

characters.name: Bad Future Stan
characters.description: Accidental Murder:it's revealed that Stan —in a fit of frustration— burnt down the Tegridy Weed farm to try and get his parents to stop arguing. However, unbeknownst to Stan, Randyhad locked Shelley in the barn for not doing her "weed chores". Stan's act of spite accidentally killed her, which also led to his momkilling herself. Amicable Exes: Wendy and Stan seem to be this as adults. Wendy is excited to see Stan and happily introduces her new husband to him, while Stan doesn't show any animosity towards Wendy and remains polite with her throughout. Awful Wedded Life: Parodied.Bad FutureStan has the latest model of Alexa, who is built to resemble a woman and is programmed to snap at him over every little flaw. Berserk Button: While he's mostly been desensitized to his father's stupidity, after having to endure being trapped with him during the COVID pandemic,everythingsurrounding him or Tegridy Farms has become his for him, to the point of burning the business down to the ground after one too manyKick the Dogmoments from Randy. Dark and Troubled Past: At some point after the pandemic (in the bad future), Stan got sick and tired of living at Tegridy Farms due to his parents' constant arguing and decided to set the weed farm on fire. Unbeknownst to him, Randy locked Shelley in a nearby barn when she didn't want to do her weed chores; Shelley wasn't able to escape the inferno. To make things worse, Sharon was so devastated by the death of her daughter that she committed suicide by shooting herself. Stan and Randy blamed each other for their family falling apart and were left estranged and miserable as a result.

characters.name: Good Future Stan
characters.description: Honorary Uncle: Following the events of the two-parts Post Covid special,Future Stan is this to Future Kyle's children. Karmic Jackpot: In the revised future, Stan is a successful Chief Master Sergeant in the U.S. Space Force and is heavily implied that his relationship with Wendy has or will be rekindled. Maybe Ever After: Considering how Wendy asks Stan to spend New Year's Eve with her and that Darwin is nowhere to be seen, it's heavily implied that Stan and Wendy are either still dating or might date again soon in the new timeline. Ridiculously Successful Future Self: Stan gets one in the revised future where he becomes a successful Master Sergeant for the US Space Force who gets to travel all over space, is anHonorary Uncleto Kyle’s children and has aMaybe Ever Afterfuture with Wendy. Ship Tease: Stan and Wendy have this in the fixed future. It's also worth noting that Wendy's husband Darwin is not in this future, possibly meaning that he never met Wendy in this timeline.

characters.name: Successful Cartman
characters.description: Cassandra Truth: Cartman's future self reallyishis future self. Of course, nobody believes him by the time he shows up and it takes its toll. Formerly Fat: Unlike the other future Cartmans, this Cartman has overcome his obesity and is physically fit. My Future Self and Me: He travels back in time to reassure his present-day self that his spur of the moment decision to turn his life around would pay off. Having just witnessed such a scenario being revealed to be a scam, present-day Cartman slags his future self off and rescinds his resolution. Ridiculously Successful Future Self: The selfish, dull-wittedSpoiled Bratsomehow managed to start his own time-travel company while simultaneously losing his excess weight. You Don't Look Like You: Aside from being physically fit, this Cartman also has a realistic nose, whereas all other future Cartmans have pig noses.

characters.name: Loser Cartman
characters.description: Did Not Think This Through: Future Cartman apparently didn't think Cartman would immediately find it suspicious that his supposed older counterpart from the future would appear to tell him to keep his life on trackafterthe parents of South Park got exposed for pulling a con on their kids with that exact concept. Naturally Cartman thinks this is a trick and decides to never change his ways, turning his future self from a thin, successful businessman to a fat, slovenly mechanic. Future Loser: Future Cartman's successes are all dashed within a second, leaving him a fat, slovenly garage worker. Karmic Transformation: For those upset that Cartman would grow up to be fit and successful after being such a terrible person, it is a relief to watch him transform into an obese, miserable mechanic. Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: Future Cartman ruins things for himself (and many other people when taking later episodes into account) when he comes to the past to congratulate his child self on making a turnaround, allowing Cartman to lose weight, become rich and successful, and run his time traveling company. Thinking he's just another Motivation Corp actor, present-day Cartman he's not going to change or think about his future after all, but continue to indulge in his obnoxious and hedonistic ways. Future Cartman then promptly turns into a fat, dirty mechanic. Real After All: At the end of the episode, Cartman announces that he actually learned a lesson from all of this and vows to turn his life around, become nicer, lose weight, etc. He is then approached by a man in a nice suit claiming to behisfuture self, who congratulates Cartman on his choice, since he considers it to be the defining moment of his life and what led him to become the rich and successful owner of a time travel business. Cartman assumes that this is just another actor, and spitefully declares that just because this asshole tried to trick him, he's now going to live his life even worse than before. After he walks

characters.name: Bad Future Cartman
characters.description: Act of True Love: To prove his devotion to his wife, Yentl, Cartman complies to Yentl's wishes and helps Stan and Kyle fixes the future, even if it may cost his happiness. Ambiguous Situation: The show initially makes it ambiguous as to whether Cartman's conversion to Judaism (including becoming a rabbi, marrying a Jewish woman, and having Jewish kids) is genuine or it's all part of a long term plan of his to get under Kyle's skin. Kyle is certain it's the latter, but Cartman's actions at the end of the episode and the following special confirm it's the former. Anti-Villain: Cartman starts as theBig Badof this special with his efforts to prevent Stan and Kyle from fixing the future, but it's only because that he's afraid that he'll lose his family if the future changes (which he did - because he remains an asshole, so it's still his fault). Became Their Own Antithesis: A raging antisemite in his childhood years grows up to become an orthodox Jewish rabbi as an adult. Disc-One Final Boss: Cartman starts off theBig Badbefore pulling aHeel–Face Turn3/4ths in where Clyde becomes theFinal Boss.

characters.name: Good Future Cartman
characters.description: Alas, Poor Villain: A non-lethal example. Stan and Kyle can't help feeling sorry for Cartman, who's now an angry, drunken, homeless wreck. His fate feels especially tragic because he sacrificed his own happy ending in the old timeline so everyone else could have theirs, and they'll never know because their old lives were erased and replaced with the new one.Stan:Man, poor Cartman.Cartman:(swigs a bottle of whiskey)Fuck youguuuuuys!You can suck mahfuckingdick!(notices Stan and Kyle)Fuck you!(flips them the bird)Kyle:It's so sad he never did anything with his life.Cartman:(continues to flip the bird)Fuck you,Kyyyyyle!Fuck you,Staaaaan!(swigs whiskey bottle)Butters:(appears next to Stan & Kyle)Hey, come on, fellas. We can't spend another holiday feeling bad for Eric. There's nothing that could have changed the path he was on.Cartman:(notices Butters)FUCK YOU, BUTTERS!(flips him off)Butters:(flips him off)FUCK YOU, ERIC!(coldly closes the blinds) The Alcoholic: Cartman's new fate in the good timeline: he's become a drunken, homeless bum who rages and insults everyone in his line of sight. Even Stan and Kyle can't help but talk about how sorry they feel for him. The Aloner: Eric Cartman becomes this in the new timeline. Once everyone, including his friends, severs their ties with Cartman, he ends up completely alone and isolated from people; as a result, he grows up to be adrunk,crazy homeless manwho’s extremely miserable. His only method of communicating with the people who used to be associated with him is to angrily curse at them, which certainly doesn’t draw them into wanting to be with him. Ambiguous Situation: Given his highly codependent relationship with his mother as a child, it's unclear whether she died in this future or if she simply kicked him out of the house. Granted, she'd likely be too old by this point to still care for her son regardless. Attention Whore: In the revised future, Cartman still tries to get as much attention as possible, loudly insulting

characters.name: Jimmy Valmer
characters.description: A crippled boy with aSpeech Impedimentand a stutter. He's also a fantastic (or so he thinks) stand-up comedian. His role in Coon and Friends is Fastpass. Abusive Offspring: He's usually quite loving with his parents, but in "Up the Down Steroid", he hits his mother on the face with one of his crutches as she tries to stop him from beating up Nancy. Acquired Situational Narcissism: In "Up the Down Steroid", his abuse of steroids turn him into an egotistical and overambitious asshole and cause him to snap at his loved ones, culminating in beating up his girlfriend and his mother. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Jimmy was born the way he was because ofthe way his parents used to make fun of crippled people.

characters.name: Clyde Donovan
characters.description: One of the 4th graders who attends South Park Elementary, and one of the dumber ones. Clyde was once described as the second fattest kid next to Cartman, which kickstarted his reputation as somewhat of aButt-Monkey. Despite this, the girls in his class once put him at #1 on their "Cutest Boys" list, if onlyjust to get free shoessince his father owns a shoe store and they wanted to justify dating him by making him look popular. His role in Coon and Friends is Mosquito. Acquired Situational Narcissism: In "The List", Clyde is listed through a list as the cutest boy by the girls, and briefly becomes arrogant and narcissistic upon finding out. After the list is exposed as a forgery, he more or less reverts to his original personality, though he slips into the role again in "Deep Learning". Aloof Ally: If he doesn't care about a particular state of affairs, he can rival Craig when it comes to his apathy.He auditions for a position as the boys' fourth friend after Kenny dies, but is honest about not really liking them anyway. When he loses, he makes sure to tell them off for their entitled behavior, but is simply dismissed as aSore Loser.He joins the boys in their mission to kill the griefer inWarcraft, only to stop playing halfway through to skim through a playboy magazine, not even warning the rest of his departure.It's also fairly obvious when he's playing a role he doesn't enjoy (such as the narrator in "Hellen Keller! The Musical", The High Elf in "The Return of the Fellowship of the Ring to the Two Towers", the Texan in "The Last of the Meheecans", and Warrior Clyde inThe Stick of Truth) vs. when he's playing one he does enjoy (such as The Lord of Darkness and Mosquito).He gives advice to The Boys on where to find theBig BadofSouth Park: Let’s Go Tower Defense Play,but he refuses to help assist on their quest, despite saidBig Badbeing an active threat to South Park. Why?Because, like Craig, he doesn’t care. He auditions for a position as the boys' fourth friend afte

characters.name: Tolkien "Token" Black
characters.description: One of the very few black kids in South Park. Tolkien is also incredibly rich. He lives in a mansion with his parents, who have well-paid jobs. His role in Coon and Friends is Tupperware. Accidental Misnaming: "The Big Fix" reveals his first name is actually "Tolkien", afterJ. R. R. Tolkien. All the times his name was previously shown as "Token" were because Cartman (and Mr. Garrison) didn't know how to spell the name accurately. Aerith and Bob: While most of the other kids have standard names, his sticks out as unusual. All of the Other Reindeer: He feels this way in "Here Comes the Neighborhood" due to the other boys mocking him for his wealth, but it's eventually subverted as the boys explain to him thatripping on him is part of being their friend, and that he would be different if theydidn'tmake fun of him.

characters.name: Craig Tucker
characters.description: One of the 4th graders who attends South Park Elementary. It's implied that he has bad behavior, and is referred to as "The biggest troublemaker" in his class by Eric Cartman in "Tweek vs. Craig". He also has a habit of flipping people off, whether to express disdain toward them or not. Acts as the leader of a rival group to The Boys called Craig's Gang at times, usually consisting of himself, Tolkien, Clyde, and Jimmy (and sometimes Tweek). His role in Coon and Friends is Super Craig. Aloof Ally: In "Pandemic", he works with the boys to get out of Peru, but spends most of his time belittling them for their constant inability to learn from their mistakes, which drives them insane. BeingThe Drag-Alongthroughout the two-parter, one can't blame him for not being too enthusiastic.Craig’s perfectly fine with telling the The Boys about where they need to go to get theBig Badof "South Park: Let’s Go Tower Defense Play", but doesn’t (canonically) tag along due to generally not caring. Craig’s perfectly fine with telling the The Boys about where they need to go to get theBig Badof "South Park: Let’s Go Tower Defense Play", but doesn’t (canonically) tag along due to generally not caring. Aloof Big Brother: Generally doesn't give his sister Tricia much attention, and even flips her off on occasion (which is a recurring tick in their family). InThe Fractured But Whole, she says that he can be a dick to her at times, butshe still ships him and Tweek together.

characters.name: Tweek Tweak
characters.description: A constantly nervous and paranoid boy with wild blond hair. He constantly twitches because of all the coffee he drinks — and because of the "healthy" sprinkling of locally brewed meth that his parents keep putting in it. He was originally an unpopular classmate of Mr. Garrison’s class who was upset about his underpants being stolen by gnomes. He served asa fifth friendfor The Boys during Season 2, andtheir new fourth friendfor a few episodes in Season 6. His role in Coon and Friends is Wonder Tweek. Abusive Parents: Not only do his parents test the quality of their meth supplies by giving it to their son through his coffee, but his father frequently jokes about selling Tweek into slavery right in front of him when it's painfully obvious his son has serious anxiety. In "Tweek x Craig", his dad admits that he's always just assumed that Tweek was a little spaz, but respects him now that he knows he's gay, which was pretty negligent on Richard's part regardless of Tweek's sexuality. EvenCartmanrealizes how messed up Tweek's home life is:Cartman: God, what the hell do his parents do to him? Aerith and Bob: Everyone has normal names, and this guy is named "Tweek".

characters.name: Jason White
characters.description: ALiving Propwho resembles actor JasonMcHugh, who starred inCannibal! The MusicalandOrgazmo, both created byTrey Parker and Matt Stone. Angry White Man:Subverted Trope. We never really get to see this side of him, despite being in a family of them. The Brute: He's unafraid to beat people up, and inThe Fractured But Whole, he reveals that he's into brutalist heroes, so the only way to get a selfie with him is to equip at least one of their abilities. The Bully: In "South Park is Gay", he's the second most antagonistic kid to Kyle, next to Craig, and the first one to get physical with him in the playground. Dramatic Irony: Jason always wished the spotlight would fall on him so he could be important.So, of course, the one time he’s given an actual major role in an episode is when he dies.

characters.name: Professor Chaos
characters.description: After being kicked out of the boy's group, Butters decides to become a villain and exact his revenge on South Park. Donning a suit of tin foil, Butters became Professor Chaos and a (highly ineffective) wave of terror will follow. Anti-Villain: His misdeeds are mildly inconvenient at worst. Also, when he assists Cartman in his schemes — he's nottryingto be actively malevolent, he's just too naive to realize/understand the consequences of his actions. Arch-Enemy: Of Mysterion and The Coon. Art Shift: InSouth Park: The Stick of TruthandSouth Park: The Fractured but Whole, he appears in anAnimesquestyle identical to the one he had in "Good Time with Weapons", causing him to look large, muscular, and threatening withMonochromatic Eyes. Benevolent Boss: He’s accommodating and friendly to nearly all of his Chaos minions, and treats them better than the superheroes treat their sidekick.

characters.name: Victor Chaos
characters.description: Affably Evil: As Victor Chaos, he has become an unscrupulous businessman whogets people to make bad investments in NFTs, but he still remains as friendly as he was as a kid, especially when he greets Stan and Kyle as they visit him in his institution cell. Bait-and-Switch: Future Butters/Victor Chaos was built up to be a complete madman, presumably aMad Scientistor perhaps aSerial Killer. Somewhat subverted because he's only a shadyNFT salesmanbut doubly subverted becausethey weren't exaggerating how dangerous he was. Co-Dragons: Both Butters and Clyde become this to Cartman, helping him try to prevent Stan and Kyle from going to the past to change the future. The Dragon: Becomes one to Rabbi Cartman. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Butters grew up to become an insane NFT peddler but still uses his ill-gotten gains to finance Kenny's scientific pursuits, still seeing him as his best friend so many years later.

characters.name: Good Future Butters
characters.description: The Dog Bites Back: While Stan and even Kyle feel bad for the pathetic state Cartman is in the good future, Butters, Cartman's biggest punching bag,dismissively tells them not to waste time feeling bad for Eric again, evensnapping back at himwhen their old dynamic reemerges.Cartman:FUCK YOU, BUTTERS!Butters:(angrily)FUCKYOU, ERIC!(coldly closes blinds) Dramatic Irony: Butters was usually the one kid who was willing to give Cartman sympathy and the benefit of doubt thanks to his naive optimism. It's only after the show's revelation that Cartman is in fact redeemable thatButters finally cuts all ties with him, deeming himBeyond Redemptionand swaying the others from taking pity on him. Meanwhile, Kyle, who originally held Cartman in deep contempt for most of the series, contrasts Butters by being sympathetic to his situation. Grew a Spine: Butters apparently grew one during his adulthood in the revised timeline, where he breaks off from his submissive role towards Cartman and cusses back at him when Cartman tries flipping him off, all while being unsympathetic towards Cartman's current predicament. Happiness in Minimum Wage: Butters is a simple waiter whose been promoted to manager in the fixed timeline, instead of a wealthy and infamousSnake Oil Salesman. That said this is still treated as Butters good future over his previous life because he still retains his sanity, maintains his friendships with almost everyone, and actually enjoys doing his job. Not Afraid of You Anymore: While Butters used to be afraid of Cartman and usually complied to his demands as a child, adult Butters in the fixed timeline no longer shows any fear towards Cartman. He merely curses back when Cartman tries flipping off Butters and closes the blinds.

characters.name: Wendy Testaburger
characters.description: The kind-hearted, bright, outspoken, integrated, leftist, liberal, and jelly school body president of the Boys' class, and Cartman's secondArch-Enemywho also has a hidden scary side, which she lets loose when you fuck with her. She's also Stan's on-and-off love interest. She breaks up with him in season 7 due to believing he was bored with her, though they get back together with him at the end of season 11. However she (reluctantly) breaks up with Stan again in Season 20 due to the other girls believing he and the boys share the sexist opinions of notorious Internet troll skankhunt42 (although they appear to be together once more inThe Fractured but Whole). Their relationship resumes in Season 26. In the video gameSouth Park: The Fractured but Whole, her superhero identity is Call Girl. Academic Athlete: She's one of the smartest kids in her class (rivaled perhaps only by Kyle) and also plays volleyball. Action Girlfriend: In "Breast Cancer Show Ever", she beats up Cartman to a bloody pulp not too many episodes after getting back together with Stan. Advertised Extra: Wendy appears in the season 27 and 28 promotional posters along with the rest of the main and supporting 4th graders, suggesting that she may keep her recurring role in those seasons. However in the seasons proper, she only appears in six out of the ten episodes, and is reduced to a background cameo in four of them.

characters.name: Bebe Stevens
characters.description: Wendy's best friend. She once hated her breasts when she started developing them early (and caused the male 4th graders to turn into perverted, mindless apes), and was once attracted to Kyle Broflovski because she thought he had a "sweet ass." Passionate like Wendy (though not very concerned with feminism and politics), she also tends to come into verbal conflict withCartman. During the period of time where her breasts were developing,Bebe would officially become a new member of The Boys, briefly replacing Cartman. She would step down soon afterwards. Abhorrent Admirer: In "Clubhouses", she's this for Kyle, constantly commenting on the shape of his ass and even passing him a note that went a little beyond flirting. On his part, though he tries to be nice to her, he's very grossed out by her (and all girls at that point), and runs off screaming when she kisses him. Aesop Amnesia: In "Bebe’s Boobs Destroy Society", Bebe had learned about how awful it can feel to beostracizedfor your breasts size, and that she wouldn’t like others only caring about her for superficial reasons like that. Around Season 8 onwards,she has no problem mocking others for their body woes(such asbeing fatorflat) andwill purposely manipulate othersfor her own self-gain. All There in the Manual:SP and Mereveals that Bebe’s first name is Barbara, while Bebe is just a nickname.

characters.name: Heidi Turner
characters.description: A kind-hearted and idealistic yet somewhat stubborn girl in the same class the four boys attend. Originally just one of the minor female classmates and a part of Wendy and Bebe's group of friends, she became a major character in Season 20 and theDeuteragonistof Season 21, where she entered an extremely complicated relationship withCartmanof all people, much to the surprise of all her friends and classmates.She's also smart and funny. Advertised Extra: Heidi Turner appears in the season 27 and 28 promotional posters along with the rest of the main and supporting 4th graders, suggesting that she may have a major or recurring role in those seasons. However in the seasons proper, she only appears in four out of the ten episodes as a non-speaking background character. Ad Hominem: Employs this tactic constantly during her stint as Cartman'sDistaff Counterpart. When Theresa briefly snipes at her, Heidi brings up her family's financial state to put her on the defensive; when Kyle attempts to implore the school to make peace, Heiditells to him shut upand accuses him of "sounding like his mom"; when Kyle rejects his friends' offer to help him search for his missing brother, Heidi accuses him of simply being bitter over being rejected by her. This last one backfires on her, however, as Kyle turns the tables anddisgustedly renounces the idea that he would ever feel any attraction for the person she had become, kick-starting herJerkass Realization. All Girls Want Bad Boys:Subverted. Yes, she does become Cartman's girlfriend, but only because he was actually very kind to her in Season 20. Thus, she did not like when he became aJerkassto her in Season 21, leading to her decision to dump Cartman in "Splatty Tomato". All-Loving Heroine: Averted in herfirst few appearancesand during her Cartmanized phase, but played straight in Season 20 and seasons 22 and beyond. Despite being part of the popular clique, Heidi takes a warm-hearted approach to anyone and everyone she can, even if sai

characters.name: RedMcArthur
characters.description: One of the minor female classmates and a part of Wendy and Bebe's group of friends. Used to be a background character more often seen with Kevin than with the other girls. Advertised Extra: The commercials made it seemed as if Red was going to have a prominent role in the "Vaccination Special", but in the actual episode Red spoke once but joined the Lil'Qties in fighting The Boys. All Women Love Shoes: Briefly dated Clyde just to get a chance at getting free shoes before passing him on to Bebe. Amicable Exes:Though she hasn't dated Clyde since "The List", she refers to him as "a goddamn dreamboat" in "Deep Learning"."Wok Is Dead" makes it clear that Red and Kevin Stoley have since ended their relationship, but they were still talking to each even inReturn of COVID, suggesting that they’re still on good terms at the least. Though she hasn't dated Clyde since "The List", she refers to him as "a goddamn dreamboat" in "Deep Learning".

characters.name: Annie Knitts
characters.description: Another tertiary student shown in 3rd/4th grade classroom over the course of the show. She's part of Wendy's group of friends, and that's really mostly it for her. Ascended Extra: Though usually just a background character in the show, she gets a major role helping the New Kid inThe Stick of Truth. She also gets a couple of speaking roles in Season 20. The Baby of the Bunch: Her few interactions with her friends show them talking to her like she's younger than them, or at least a bit lower in the social scale. Because You Were Nice to Me: Though the pleases and sparkles group generally doesn't allow boys, she gets the New Kid to meet up with them after they save her from a gang of bullies. Beware the Nice Ones: Despite her naivete, she showed a lot of leadership for the girls to get revenge on the boys for assumptions that one of them is the notorious Internet troll in "Skank Hunt", and she kickstarts the mass breakup in school by handing a breakup note to her boyfriend Daniel.

characters.name: Nichole Daniels
characters.description: The newest girl in the 4th grade. Although she initially shows interest in Kyle, Cartman's manipulation leads to her realizing that Tolkien is the one that she wants. Alliterative Name: One of Nichole’s alter egos is calledNymphNichole. Apologises a Lot: In her debut episode, though she appears to have dropped this habit in her subsequent appearances. Ascended Extra: Following her debut episode, she was mostly relegated to the background and remained a supporting character, until Season 20 onwards where she gradually became one of the most prominent girls in the class, even surpassing Wendy and Bebe in terms of screentime in Season 22 and 23. Birds of a Feather: As it turns out, she's one with Tolkien, not because they're both black, but because they're both self-conscious about people finding them weird for being aToken Minority Couple.

characters.name: Betsy
characters.description: Ascended Extra:Downplayed. She was originally a side character who appeared once per season with occasional lines, but seasons 26 and 27 would start to lend her more screentime, and "Deep Learning" establishes her as being close to the popular girls. Badass Biker: She seems to be trying to emulate this look, wearing a leather jacket with jeans and a white shirt. Bows for Cuteness: Her bow contrasts her otherwise tomboyish and rude demeanor by adding a small layer of cuteness. Boyish Short Hair: Befitting her toughness, Betsy wears her hair very short. Conspiracy Theorist: She made her debut as one of the Lil' QtiesnoteThe youth wing ofQAnon, having been lead to believe the vaccines against COVID-19 can't be trusted.

characters.name: Scott Malkinson

characters.name: Kevin Stoley
characters.description: A minor background character in the Boys' class and a fan ofStar WarsandStar Trek. He's usually unimportant, but joined Cartman's pirate crew in "Fatbeard". characters.name: Bradley Biggle
characters.description: A mild-mannered,attractivefourth grader and the younger brother ofHenrietta. His role in Coon and Friends isAmerica's favorite superhero, Mintberry Crunch. Alliterative Name:Goes along with some superheroes' alter-egos. Ascended Extra: Becomes one for the "Coon and Friends" trilogy, despite being essentially a background character before that point. Barrier Warrior: His "Protective Berry Bubble" power. It's even part of his abilities inThe Fractured But Whole, where it's shown that he can grant his allies temporary invincibility by cleansing them with Mint while covering his enemies with Berry, nullifying all damage from enemy attacks.

characters.name: Bill Allen and FosseMcDonald
characters.description: Two bullies that find everything to be "gay". Aerith and Bob: Bill's name is a little more standard than his friend's. Sometimes they have quick line in the background just point out the gayness of a situation,truly informative. characters.description: Academic Alpha Bitch: An A+ student who starts a cloning war with Kyle. Adaptational Dumbass:Zig-Zagged. He continually goads Kyle after the fact, while propping up his ego about his ability (or rather, his father’s ability) to create a human clone, leading to the Kyle and Cartman completely ignoring Stan’s own problems. Finally, when the clone is eventually created and clearly rabid, it’s HIS fault that the clone gets out andeventually destroys the town,which he is fully aware of and apathetic about. Even when he and his father eventually track the clone,he shows no concern over it potentially harming The Boys and simply demands they give him back.

characters.name: Brimmy
characters.description: A third-grade classmate of the boys, then a recurringLiving Prop. Flat Character: He was the only third-grade classmate to never get a speaking role. characters.description: A minor female classmate part of Wendy and Bebe's group of friends and a member of the Pleases & Sparkles club. All Women Love Shoes: She conspired with the girls to put Clyde at number one on their cutest boys list just to get free shoes from him. characters.description: A girl part of the Pleases & Sparkles club, and is best friends with Lola above. She's mostly another minor female classmate, but had an important role in "Bass to Mouth". Beauty Is Never Tarnished: Subverted in "Bass to Mouth", when she shits her pants in front of everyone. For most of the episode, she presents herself as a serious high-ranking member of thePleases and Sparklesclub, before dropping the mask and becoming more callous when Wendy starts digging too deep in the matter. Blackmail: Jenny’s plan to keep Wendy quiet aboutthe list’s tamperingwas to frame Wendy as the school’s biggest liar (or at least the biggest one among the Pleases & Sparkles club).

characters.name: Millie Larsen

She's also this in "Bebe's Boobs Destroy Society" and "Marjorine", as she participates in slut shaming Bebe and ostracizing Marjorine respectively but doesn't say anything meaningful beyond muttering "slut" at the former and frowning at the latter. It's All About Me: Upon her friend request to The New Kid inSouth Park: The Stick of Truthall her dialogue specifically revolves around her being narcissistic about her interview.

characters.name: Lisa Berger
characters.description: Another new 4th grade character that appeared in Season 16. She becomes more of a focus in the Season 17 finale, "The Hobbit". Abhorrent Admirer: Butters was turned off by her being too fat, but suddenly gained interest once Wendy photoshopped Lisa to make her look thin and attractive. Age-Inappropriate Dress: The bikini she wears during "Work Out, Slut". Ascended Extra: Introduced as a random child being ridiculed in "Butterballs", but winds up on the cheerleading team in Season 17, leading up to her role in the finale. Big Beautiful Woman:Played with. While she’s ridiculed for her weight at first, once Wendy Photoshops a picture of her nearly all of the guys want her, though they’re under the assumption that she’s thin and beautiful. Lisa later tries toinvoke this trope herselfby wearing arevealing dominatrix-esque outfitfor her song "Work Out, Slut".

characters.name: Damien Thorn
characters.description: Satan's son who was sent to South Park Elementary to destruct the school's property. He was hated on for being the son of the devil, but it turned out he just wanted to be treated equally like the other kids. Adaptational Heroism: In both versions ofThe Omen, while Damien is ratherAmbiguously Evil, he's still bizarrely demented for a little kid. Damien is alotmore agreeable here, and isn't all too jazzed about being the Antichrist. Anti-Anti-Christ: All the kids at school hated him for being Satan's son and showing off evil characteristics, but he just wanted acceptance after all. The Cameo: He's the main antagonist ofReligious HorrorfilmThe Omen, and he shows up in South Park. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Damien has been MIA since Season 21’s "SUPER HARD PCness", which was back in November 2017. Slightly lessened if we include his poster in the Nintendo Switch version ofFractured But Whole, which would mean his last appearance was August 2018.

characters.name: Gregory of Yardale
characters.description: An English boy who transferred to South Park from Yardale. The Ace: He had a 4.0 grade point average during his attendance at school in Yardale. He seems to be far more competent in leading the revolt than Stan as shown in the La Resistance meeting at Carl's Warehouse. Character Development: A subtle example. The first time he tries to give the class a political lecture, he comes across as a buzzkill and is ignored by everyone except Wendy, and later it's Cartman who briefly gets everyone to listen to him by singingKyle's Mom is a Bitch. The second time, he seems to have learnt from this and sways everyone to his side by singingLa Resistance, motivating the entire team to action. Child Prodigy: Even more well-versed in politics than Wendy, and a superb skater and student. Dude Where Is My Respect: For his work in assembling La Resistance and helping save Terrance & Phillip, he's rewarded with Wendy going back to Stan and saying "Fuck (Gregory) right in the ear".

characters.name: Mark and Rebecca Cotswolds
characters.description: Two homeschooled children who develop an interest in attending real elementary school after meeting the other South Park kids. Beware the Nice Ones: Despite spending most of the episode getting pushed around, Mark proves he has some bite by beating up Kyle for supposedly corrupting his sister. Bubble Boy: The first time Mark arrives to elementary school, he goes in a giant hamster ball. Character Tics: Rebecca bites her lips and clasps her hands together in most of her scenes. When she spells, she whispers the letters into her hand first. Child Prodigy: Both of them are incredibly smart, spelling complicated words at the spelling bee without a care. Rebecca is also able to replicate brain surgery despite being only eight.

characters.name: Gary Harrison, Jr.
characters.description: The first Mormon character onSouth Park. He tries to befriend Stan fairly quickly. The Ace: Is both smart and athletic, doesn't let the other kids' teasing get to him, and probably the nicest kid, nay,person, in all of South Park. All-Loving Hero: Arguably the nicest character in the entire series, able to forgive teasing or threats, and see the good side to everything. The Anti-Nihilist: His last line implies that he doesn't actually believe in the supernatural claims of Mormonism (or is at best agnostic to them); but still follows it because it makes him and his family happy and good. Badass Pacifist: He's state champion in wrestling, but never thinks of fighting anyone and is content with getting beat up by Stan if it boosts the latter's social status.

characters.name: David Rodriguez
characters.description: David is a Mexican-American student introduced in Season 19. Demoted to Extra: He becomes aLiving Propafter Season 19 and has not spoken since that season. Early-Bird Cameo: He makes his debut in "The Last of the Meheecans" as a Mexican child trying to break a Mantequilla pinata. He also had a non-speaking cameo as a Syrian refugee child during Kyle's speech at the end of "Stunning and Brave". Flat Character: At least so far. Living Prop: He only makes background appearances in episodes after Season 19, as stated inDemoted to Extra.

characters.name: Charlotte
characters.description: A Canadian girl that Butters met and was forced to date in order to give her a "Hot Cosby." Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Mixed withUncertain Doom. The last we see of her, she breaks up with Butters in season 20. When Canada got nuked in season 21, it's unknown if Charlotte was a casualty or not. This could serve asLaser-Guided Karmafor unfairly breaking up with Butters. Girlfriend From Canada:Subverted, as she literally was this to Butters. Kick the Dog: The way shebreaks up with Buttersover something that doesn't even affect them comes off as particularly cruel, and leads directly toButters escalating the gender war. Official Couple: She enters a long-distance relationship with Butters.Too bad it doesn't last.

characters.name: Sophie Gray
characters.description: A new girl from Scottsdale. She has diabetes and likesThe Mandalorian. Due to her having diabetes, she instantly becomes the target of Scott Malkinson's affections. Class Princess: Despite her diabetes, she quickly becomes popular at school. But she is also very kind and has no hidden meanness. Dude Magnet: Her interest in all thingsStar Wars-related (barring the latest trilogy), causes every boy in school to try and court her, much to Scott's chagrin. She even manages to start a rivalry between the otherwise tightly-knit goth kids. Fangirl: One of the first things she mentions when introducing herself is her love forStar Wars,especiallyThe Mandalorian,which she tries to watch with Scott. Foil: ToScott Malkinson. Sophie is a respected student that nearly every boy is interested in, Scott is often treated asThe Friend Nobody Likesand aButt-Monkey, who’s only second to Butters and Pip.

characters.name: Dougie O'Connell
characters.description: Younger nerdier friend of Butters. Joins the latter in his quest to destroy the world after being rejected by the other kids, under the alias of Professor Chaos' minion, General Disarray. All of the Other Reindeer: He was rejected by the boys without even getting to know him in "Professor Chaos", and inSouth Park: The Stick of Truth, Cartman forbid him from joining his kingdom because he was "too ginger", thoughButtersstill allowed him a spot as a squire. Anti-Villain: He's more savvy than his boss, but he's still a first grader who is way over his head, and usually too subservient toButtersto be much of a threat on his own. Ascended Extra: Though he's a minor character in the show, he has five cards inSouth Park: Phone Destroyer. Blind Without 'Em: Implied inSouth Park: Phone Destroyer. After he's defeated in Stage 24 and his defeat animation shows him losing his glasses, he sends a misspelled message in the group chat saying he can't find them.

characters.name: Christophe "Ze Mole"
characters.description: A bitter French nine-year-old boy with an intense hatred of God. An expert in covert operations. Back from the Dead: Although it's only a blink-and-you'll-miss-it shot, he makes a reappearance in "Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub" where he's shown onLate Night with Conan O'Brienwhile Stan flips through channels. This implies that he was resurrected after Kenny's wish inThe Moviefor everything to go back to normal. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Has noticeably thicker eyebrows than most of the characters. Died in Your Arms Tonight:He dies in Kyle's arms. Expy: Suspiciously similar to Grantaire fromLes Misérables. His death also brings to mind that of Eponine from the same musical.

characters.name: Nelson Brown
characters.description: An ill-fated member of the Pee Wee hockey team. Nelson has terminal cancer, but tries his best to stay positive, even as it's clear he doesn't have long to live. Death by Despair: He succumbs to his illness when his team loses. "No hope..." Determinator: He's clearly weak from his cancer when we first meet him, and seems to be going through chemotherapy, but is still playing hockey. He soon gets worse, though, and eventually has to be hospitalized. Littlest Cancer Patient: He soon ends up in the hospital when his cancer becomes terminal, and really wants Stan to win the big game for him. Sadly, he dies when he sees his team lose to the Red Wings.

characters.name: Bridon Gueermo
characters.description: A third grader who has seenHigh School Musicalover 100 timesand is an extremely talented singer and dancer. Despite this, singing and dancing aren't his hobbies; he really wants to play basketball. Abusive Parents: His dad always beats him up for choosing to be a basketball player instead of a singer and dancer until the end of his episode. His mom, however, is an aversion and tries her best to protect him from his dad's cruel punishments and ridicules. The Ace: There doesn't appear to be anything he's bad at. Despite hating musical theater because his father forced him into it, his mere presence (and the kids'High School Musicalfandom) causes the other studentsto spontaneously break into song and dance. All the girls like him despite him being a year younger, and he can shoot free throws effortlessly. On the other hand, he's anExtreme Doormatuntil the climax of his episode. Ambiguously Bi: Despite all the girls gusing over him, he returns no interest in them whatsoever (though this could be because singing and dancing aren't his true hobbies). Furthermore, his last name Gueermo is pronounced and spelled similarly to "Queermo"notea mashup of the words "queer" and "homo", and his dad shows off several effeminate characteristics. Though, a cut sidequest inThe Stick of Truthhas him telling the New Kid to give Annie a letter from him, saying that he has a thing for her and he cannot get her out of his mind. Arch Nemesis Dad: He hates that his father won’t let him play basketball and that he abuses him and his mother.

characters.name: Kip Drordy
characters.description: A boy who felt lonely for being a friendless Facebook user. That was, until Kyle sent him a friend request. Butt-Monkey: An outcast that nobody wanted to be friends with due to his geeky nature. This is later shown in "Butterballs", where he serves as the director of Stan's anti-bullying music video. Cool Kid-and-Loser Friendship: Develops one with Kyle after he felt sympathetic for him having no friends throughout his six months on Facebook. Unfortunately, this causes Kyle to lose his popularity amonghisfriends. Fat Idiot:Downplayed Trope. He’s only a little heavy and isn’t really dumb, he just hashorrific social skills. No Social Skills: Kip seems to treat getting an online friend as being equal to a real one and treats a photo of Kyle as being as the same as the real deal. It comes to the point where he tries to feed it popcorn and go to the movies with it.

characters.name: Gordon Stolski
characters.description: A third-grader and ginger kid who runs the morning announcements. He used to be a member of Cartman’s ginger movement before Cartman disbanded the organization. All for Nothing:The entire reason Gordon Stolski was killed was because he was mistaken for a trucker who had previously wronged the intruder, the intruder kills himself soon afterwards, meaning not only did Stolski and an unknown victim die for nothing, but the intruder as well. Ate His Gun:The intruder forces him to put the barrel of his gun in his mouth, then pulls the trigger. Butt-Monkey: All of his appearances saw him get the short end of the stick. Due to the Dead: He's given a memorial service in "Ginger Kids" hosted by Mackey, and his photo can still be seen in the "Hall of Honor" as late asSouth Park: The Fractured But Whole.

characters.name: Tammy Warner
characters.description: Kenny's one-time girlfriend, who once gave another boy a"BJ"in the parking lot of a T.G.I. Friday's after listening to the Jonas Brothers. Fangirl: Is one ofThe Jonas Brothers, and so she has Kenny wear a purity ring once they start to promote them. She has not appeared in the series since Season 16's "Faith Healing", though she appears inSouth Park: The Fractured but WholeandSouth Park: Snow Day!. The Dog Bites Back: Or "the cat claws back". In "Faith Healing", Cartman hits her with a toy, and she responds by clawing at his face and hissing. Formally Named Pet: Her name isMr.Kitty. Gender Bender: Was shown to befemaleinCat Orgy, but was shown again as a functional male inMajor Boobage. Because of this, she is later confirmed to be ahermaphrodite.

characters.name: Fluffy
characters.description: Eric Cartman's pet pig. Animals Not to Scale: Like most fictional potbellied pigs, Fluffy is depicted as the size of a piglet, being much smaller than thePint-Sized Boysto the point where Cartman can easily carry her around with no effort. Bad People Abuse Animals: Despite being protective of her in her first appearance, Cartman smacks Fluffy in "Cherokee Hair Tampons" after she wakes him up. Bestiality Is Depraved: Was impregnated by Mr. Garrison and gave birth to a piglet with his face. But Liquor Is Quicker: Given alcohol by the boys in an attempt to crossbreed her and Kyle's elephant.

characters.name: Extended Cartman Family
characters.description: Eric Cartman's maternal relatives, which includes his grandmother Mabel, grandfather Harold, great-grandmother Florence, aunt Lisa, uncles Howard, Stinky and Fat Bob, and cousins Alexandra, Fred, and Elvin. Uncle Howard breaks out of prison with Charlie Manson, which kickstarts the episode's main plot. All Relatives Share a Surname: For some reason, Florence shares the Cartman surname with her married daughter Mabel. Annoying Younger Sibling: Rather Annoying Younger Cousin, but Eric is not too pleased when he is asked to take care of his little cousin Elvin by their grandmother. Big, Thin, Short Trio: Between the three children there’s the tall and thin Alexandra, the short and stubby Elvin, and Eric, the fattest of the three. Birds of a Feather: Almost all of Cartman's relatives are exactly like Cartman, to the point that they all act like him and use his catchphrases. Notably, Liane can clearly be seen and heard saying, "Aww, weak!" in unison with the rest of the family when the football broadcast returns after the news report on Charlie Manson's escape.

Close friends of the Marshes and Broflovskis, but not well-developed. Abusive Parents: Both physically and emotionally. They later confirm this themselves). Alliterative Name:StephenStotch.

characters.description: Butters' aunt and uncle who live in Los Angeles. Adults Are Useless: They know immediately that AWESOM-O is just Cartman in disguise, but don't realize Butters doesn't know this and despite knowing Cartman hasn't eaten anything for days they don't try to feed him or show much concern for him. Creepy Uncle: Despite appearing to be friendly and good with kids, Butters mentions in a later episode that his uncle sexually abused him. Depraved Bisexual: He’s married to Nellie and mostly had some intercourse with her, but he also molested Butters at some. Plus all theDomestic Abusewith his wife can't be too healthy either. "The Poor Kid" addressed this but ended with him getting his kids back. They don't even remember the meetings because they spent the entire time drunk, something Mysterion finds entirely plausible.This somehow wound up with Carol being chosen to birth "the spawn of Cthulhu". Butt-Monkey: Even ignoring his awful living conditions and marriage (both of which he's also partly responsible for), most episodes that prominently feature Stuart show him getting beaten up by his family members or friends, humiliated, or both. Examples are "Chickenpox", "Cartman Joins NAMBLA", "The Poor Kid", and "The City Part of Town". Must run in the family.

characters.name: KarenMcCormick
characters.description: Kenny's adorable little sister. Big Brother Worship: All the things Kenny does for her do not go unnoticed. She considers him to be her best friend, and also sees Mysterion as her guardian angel. As an adult, she sports a necklace with Mysterion's symbol, showing her devotion hasn't faded with time. Children Are Innocent: She's one of the very few child characters onSouth Parkwho hasn't committed acts of violence. That says a lot. Corrupt the Cutie: Mysterion fears that this is what hanging out with the Vamp kids will do to her inSouth Park: The Fractured but Whole, but his efforts to stop them only makes things worse. In the end, she starts to hang out with Henrietta, who teaches her how to be goth by smoking a cigarette and acting rude and gloomy all the time.Mysterion:Well, at least she's not a vamp kid. The Cutie: An adorable little girl with a high, squeaky voice.

characters.name: KevinMcCormick
characters.description: Kenny's seemingly slow older brother with a slurred speech pattern. Abusive Offspring: Kevin once fought his dad, Stuart, after he goaded him, though if Carol is correct, it might have been because he was drunk. Adaptational Intelligence: Kevin’s able to articulate his words a lot better inPhone Destroyer, this could be justified by the fact that he’s a playing a character as Infiltrator Kevin, or due to him seemingly not drinking any alcohol. The Alcoholic: In "The Poor Kid", his mother implies that he too is a heavy drinker, and refers to him and his father as "drunk pieces of shit". Aloof Big Brother: He had a laugh with Kenny on occasion and once went on a roller coaster with him, but besides that he does not seem to get involved with his siblings, and unlike Kenny, doesn't seem to look out for Karen much.

characters.name: Grandma Tucker
characters.description: Craig's grandmother, who gave him $100 for his birthday. Doting Grandparent: Gave her grandson a check for $100 for his birthday. Small Role, Big Impact: While she has a very minor role and is only shown in a photograph, the check she gave her grandson ends up being used to be invested in a Peruvian flute band, which kickstarts the episode's plot.

characters.name: Stripe
characters.description: Craig's pet guinea pig. Morality Pet: Even before Craig was characterized by hisDeadpan Snarkertendencies, he was shown to hold Stripe in high regard as his prized guinea pig. Replacement Goldfish: It was revealed inThe Fractured But Wholethat Craig has had 4 guinea pigs named Stripe; the Stripe he has now (Stripe #4) was given to him by his boyfriend, Tweek, presumably because the other ones either died or ran away. Stripe #1 died when Craig's mom accidentally stepped on him, and broke his back. Craig suspects his dad of poisoning Stripe #3 after he pooped in the dining room. It is also revealed that Stripe #3 died very recently, due to the fact that Craig still has (#3)'s toys and food dish tucked away in his closet.

characters.name: Steve and Linda Black
characters.description: Tolkien’s rich parents. All Men Are Perverts: Steve was already aware of which pornoBackdoor Sluts 9was in "The Return of the Fellowship of the Ring to the Two Towers". Always Someone Better: When Steve starts his own marijuana farm, he completely upstages Randy as Steve not only produces great weed himself, but he also actually knows how to run a business competently and has the advantage of being able to serve customers who want to support black-owned businesses. Ascended Extra: In Season 25 and the Streaming Wars specials, Steve is promoted from being just one of the dads to a major character; entering a rivalry with Randy, going toe-to-toe withPi Pi, and revealing unique traits such as being a huge Lord of the Rings fanatic. As his wife, Linda also gets a little more focus. Black and Nerdy: Steve is a bigJ. R. R. Tolkienfan and named Tolkien after him.

characters.name: Mrs. Stevens
characters.description: Bebe's mother. A large-chested, stereotypical dumb blonde. Ambiguously Absent Parent: For a while her husband, Bebe's dad, isn't mentioned, though we'd guess he's probably around, considering the "Mrs.Stevens". EventuallyAvertedin later seasons where Bebe is seen with both parents frequently. Animate Body Parts: It's implied her breasts talk on their own like Bebe's, as Ms. Stevens doesn't react when a shocked Bebe tells her about it, and if she's to be taken at her word, it happens to every woman. Be a Whore to Get Your Man: Relied on her looks rather than her intelligence and personality to get through life. Big-Breast Pride: She encourages Bebe to not be ashamed of having breasts, even if they take a life of their own and start conspiring to enslave all the boys.

characters.name: Betsy Donovan
characters.description: Clyde's mother, she often emotionally abuses Clyde for leaving the toilet seat up. Abusive Parents: Initially not the case for her, until in her final appearance where she repeatedly humiliates and emotionally abuses Clyde for leaving the toilet seat up.While she is dying, she apologizes to Clydefor not being harder on him. All for Nothing:Her death and all the fuss it instigated ended up being for naught when Sir. John Harrington's ghost reveals that he invented the toilet intending people to sit on it backwards, which would've prevented her from falling in had she known that. To add insult to injury, Clyde continues to leave the toilet seat up out of stubbornness, spitting on the face of herLast Request.Lampshadedby Cartman.Cartman:I know you've had a tough week, Clyde, but at least your mom didn't die for nothing. I mean, we're kinda right back at the bathroom being the last bastion of American freedom, so technically, your momdiddie for nothing. Asshole Victim:She dies brutally in a toilet accident in the episode that portrays her at her worst, and her only regret is not having been harsher on Clyde than she already was. At the end of the episode, Clyde certainly seems to have lost all respect for her, as he continues to leave the toilet seat up just to spite her ghost, but several of his lines fromThe Fractured But Wholeimply that he does mourn her. Complexity Addiction: Her response to Clyde putting the toilet seat up is to get him back into the bathroom, berate him over his habit, and make him put the seat down. Arguably even more so when she goes to his school just to get him to put the seat down when he does it again.

characters.name: Roger Donovan
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: Though he's one of the least prominent parents, he gets a supporting role in "Not Suitable For Children". Henpecked Husband: Roger can't manage to get Betsy to calm down about Clyde leaving the toilet seat up. He also takes a backseat to Clyde's education after he starts dating Janice, who soon begins to influence Clyde on her own. Horrible Judge of Character: According to Clyde in "Pajama Day", he fell forMatt Damon's crypto ad and "lost all his fuckin' money". If the celebrity put as much enthusiasm in that add as he did for hisPiPi+commercial, then that's all on Roger. Only Sane Man: Compared to most of the other parents and family members, he is one of the more reasonable ones as he is a decent parental figure to Clyde and hasn’t been showing any negative traits so far, though there are occasions where he shows someParental Obliviousnessat certain situations. Out of Focus: He rarely shows up and has pretty muchno characterization.

characters.name: Janice
characters.description: Clyde's stepmother who started dating Roger afterBetsy's death. Affably Evil: She's a sweet girlfriend towards Roger while making a genuine effort to be aGood Stepmotherto Clyde, even if she’s willing to use influencers to manipulate children and later kill them off, just to get Clyde’s views. Bad Boss: After hiring LoganLeDoucheto peddle and advertise Cred, she has him killed when he becomes a threat to Clyde finding out her role in the scheme. The fact that Clyde finds out soon thereafter regardless means his death wasAll for Nothingin the grand scheme of things, but she doesn't seem to care. The Bad Guy Wins: In the end, Janice gets exactly what she wants; getting Clyde to call her mom. The fact that Clyde is cursing at her while doing so does nothing to deter her joy. Bait-and-Switch: At the end of the episode, Clyde asks her if he can call her Mom. She's obviously very flattered as she's spent the whole episode trying to parent him. He uses what would normally be a sweet moment in any other context to shout "Fuck you, Mom!"

characters.name: Ryan and Sarah Valmer
characters.description: The Ditz: Ryan is shown to not have much awareness or common sense, such as in "Night of the Living Homeless" where his idea for dealing with all the homeless people is to just make them easier to look at by giving them all designer sleeping bags and makeovers. Emergency Services: Ryan is the chief of the South Park Fire Department. Good Parents: They're usually shown to care about Jimmy's well-being a lot, such as expressing concern about him being in a gang. Laser-Guided Karma: They claim Jimmy to have been born the way he is because they used to make fun of disabled people in high school. Or in Ryan's own words, Jimmy was "sent to them through the vengeful and angry hand of God to teach them a lesson." One-Steve Limit:Averted. There's also a kid in "Taming Strange" who has the same name as Ryan, but the former is only a one-shot character in that episode.

characters.name: Richard and Helen Burch
characters.description: Timmy's parents, who have the same disability as their son. Good Parents: They're more than happy to indulge in Timmy's love of rock music, as they attend his concerts. One-Shot Character: As of Season 26 and not counting their cameo at the 2020 Broncos game, their only appearance has been in "Timmy 2000". Out of Focus: We see them the least out of any parents that are known to be in the picture. They were absent for numerous parent-heavy occasions, such as "Child Abduction is Not Funny". Strong Family Resemblance: Between the two, it's clear that Timmy inherited most of his looks from Helen, and he dresses like a mini version of Richard. Of note, both of Timmy's parents are left-handed, while Timmy is right-handed (look at which side their wheelchair controls are on).

characters.description: Bridon'sabusive father, who is obsessed with Broadway musicals. Domestic Abuse: He slaps his wife and son over even the slightest contradiction. Fantasy-Forbidding Father: A parody of this trope; he wants his son to be a musical theatre star, but Bridon would rather play basketball. Heel–Face Turn: He eventually comes around when he's forced to watch his son's basketball game with his wife, seeing the musical aspects and choreographed cheering of the crowd and starts taking part in it.

characters.name: Crystal White

First he shows up at night to scare her for no reason in "Splatty Tomato", and then he has his bodyguard Mr. Service violently tackle her while kidnapping the family in "The Vaccination Special", even though Crystal wasn't doing anything. Girlish Pigtails: Crystal’s a young little girl, who has small pigtails at the ends of her hair.

characters.name: Clark Malkinson
characters.description: Scott Malkinson's father. He works for a cable company. Abusive Parents: Just like Cartman, he makes fun of his own son's lisp and diabetes. Everyone Has Standards: He belittles his own son for being diabetic, but hates Mr. Garrison just as much as everyone else. Evil Luddite: He hates modern streaming services likeNetflix,Hulu, andDisney+, and is willing to read the riot act to and ridicule his son over simply demanding to sign up for Disney+. He even gathers a group of cable repairmen to sabotage South Park's access to streaming services just so he and his coworkers can hold their jobs as cable technicians. He also loves to tout that cable television is better than streaming services to his wife and his clientele. Fat Bastard: Quite paunchy and never shown in an endearing light.

characters.name: Mrs. Mackey
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: She returns in Season 25 after nearly 20 years of absence. Cool Old Lady: Mr. Mackey's mom seems like a kind lady who cares about her son, even keeping his room the way it was. She later helps Mackey realize what he's doing is wrong and gives him a much-needed talk to help him move on from his nostalgia trip. Strong Family Resemblance: Mr. Mackey's mom looks very identical to him, with a very large head and a very skinny body. Shared Family Quirks: Mr. Mackey's mom has "m'kay" as herVerbal Tic, just like her son.

characters.name: Mr. Garrison Sr.
characters.description: Mr. Garrison's father. Abusive Parents: Averted and parodied with Mr. Garrison's dad. The beginning of the episode makes it seem like he traumatized Mr. Garrison by molesting him. However, Mr. Garrison was traumatized because his fatherdidn'tmolest him, making him feel unloved. Aren't You Going to Ravish Me?: Mr. Garrison has gotten it into his head that getting molested is a sign of being loved, and since his fathernevermolested him, then it means he doesn't love him. Throughout the episode, Garrison even tries to entice his father into coming for him. Hidden Backup Prince: Parodied with what we first hear about Mr. Garrison's relationship with his father, with the former being pressed about"a demon hiding in his closet" trying to "compromise" his family(in the relayed words of Mr. Mackey), and then (poorly) invoked by obviously non-royal Mr. Garrison himself, who claims he was too busy philandering and doing (commoner) whores around the block to ever have anyclose-contactrelationship with him. Only Sane Man: Between his wife and his son, he's the only one to see anything wrong with molesting his son.

characters.name: Thomas and NellieMcElroy
characters.description: Chef's parents, who live in Scotland. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: They embarrass their son Chef. Ambiguous Situation: Did they or didn't they pass away between their final on-screen appearance and their son's death? Bait-and-Switch:Thomas' first story about encountering the Loch Ness Monster. It builds up as some harrowing experience, until he says the monster asked him for money. Specifically $3.50.Thomas tells Randy and Sharon the story of hisAlien Abduction, but the twist is that the Loch Ness Monster faked it to get more money from him.At the pre-wedding dinner, Thomas tells a story about a young Chef, which seems like it will be a heartwarming story, but it immediately trails off into yet another Loch Ness Monster story, who pretended to be Chef's imaginary friend to badger Thomas for money. Thomas' first story about encountering the Loch Ness Monster. It builds up as some harrowing experience, until he says the monster asked him for money. Specifically $3.50.

characters.name: Alexis Testaburger and Mr. Testaburger
characters.description: Adults Are Useless: They do care for Wendy but at times, they’re useless in Wendy’s struggles. Instances include Mr. Testaburger bringing Wendy into the “whore” trend Paris Hilton influences in “Stupid Spoiled Whore Video Playset” and “Breast Cancer Show Ever” where they refuse to let Wendy fight Cartman, even though the latter is clearly bullying her. Depending on the Writer: Their competence really depends on the episode plot. In episodes “Bebe’s Boobs Destroy Society” and “Dances With Smurfs”, they are shown to be concerned for Wendy as Alexis doesn’t want the former to painfully give herself breast implants in the former episode and Mr. Testaburger questions Wendy’s crisis in the latter episode after Butters pees on their house. Other episodes like “Stupid Spoiled Whore Playset” and “Breast Cancer Show Ever” however have them be completely useless in Wendy’s struggles and apathetic to her well-being. No Name Given: Neither of their names are revealed when they debut. However, Alexis's name is revealed inThe End of Obesitywhile Mr. Testaburger's name remains a mystery. Out of Focus: The least focused parents. Most of the time, they're mainly just in the background without any acknowledgement. Heck, Mr. Testaburger's name isn't even revealed at this point. Parents as People: They do care about Wendy but, they are also clearly shown to not be able to see when certain situations genuinely hurt Wendy and generally seem oblivious to how the "Whore" trend and Cartman's bullying makes her suffer. They don't even let Wendy explain herself when Cartman pulls aWounded Gazelle Gambitto get her in trouble. And whether they're aware or not and/or were involved or not with theunknown traumatic incidentWendy mentioned having to go through in "Deep Learning" is anyone's guess.

characters.name: PC Babies
characters.description: The product of a brief affair between PC Principal and Strong Woman. Riley, Bailey, Harper, River, and Emory are a set of quintuplets currently being raised by their mother and (unacknowledged, due to the social stigma surrounding workplace relationships) father. They are extremely PC. Child Popstar: To an extreme. They aren't even a year old and yet they've formed a band/brand worth over 100 million dollars. Child Prodigy: They're infants with an understanding of critical theory and social justice; not to mention the fact that they're able to outsmart their distracted parents and roam around town unsupervised. Expy: Their theme song andabrupt prominencehighlights them as expies ofthe Muppet babiesand the broaderSpin-Off Babiestrend of the late 80s-early 90s. Ironically, they'renotthe trope they're parodying because they'rethe identical offspring of an existing character, not the child versions of him. Gendered Genetics: Zigzagged; the three male PC Babies inherited their father's dirty blond hair and blue eyes, but so did the two female babies. Justified, however, since darker hair tends to defeat lighter hair in the gene pool, and PC Principal's hair is indeed darker than Strong Woman's. Additionally, we don't know if Strong Woman has blue eyes or not due to theSouth Parkartstyle not rendering any character with a proper eye colour.

characters.name: Randy Marsh
characters.description: Stan's dad, a geologist (and thus the only non-madscientist in South Park; sometimes) turned cannabis farmer. Deficient in common sense, but makes up for it with great passion and enthusiasm for... well, whatever happens to be the focus of the episode. The de facto leader of the town whenever they face a threat. He tends to be the main character in storylines involving the adults of South Park, and thus is the adult figure that most interacts with the boys in the main plot. Abusive Dad: If there was any doubt before, he's become very much this of the emotional kind once the family moves to Tegridy Farms. He constantly belittles his family for not wanting to be involved in the business and ignores their own activities and needs in favour of getting high. It gets to the point where Stan and Shelley are positively gleeful about the prospect of Randy being given a lengthy prison sentence. Accidental Hero: In "The Losing Edge", his multiple drunkenCock Fightswith the dads of his son's opposing baseball teams end up saving the boys from having to spend the entire summer playing baseball (which they hated) when his fight with Bat-Dad gets them disqualified by proxy. This actually marks one of the few times where Stan has praised him for something. Addled Addict: Aside from alcoholism, Randy tends to develop an addiction to whatever drugs are trending at the time. The Alcoholic: Not quite as bad as Stuart, but he is frequently shown drunk. The plot of "Bloody Mary" focuses on him going to A.A., though they are useless, teaching him he is powerless to the "disease of alcoholism". Encouraged by Stan, he tries to learn discipline and self-control, but he continues to have unhealthy drinking habits, though he is in complete denial over having a drinking problem when confronted.

characters.name: Sharon Marsh
characters.description: Stan's mom, who is much saner than her husband. Not that it says much. Angst Coma: She was so traumatized by9/11that in its immediate aftermath she spent three weeks on the couch watchingCNNnonstop. Anti-Villain: InThe Movie, she refused to take accountability for letting Stan watchTerrance & Phillipmovie and becoming more crude as a result, instead blaming it all on Canada for allowing such movies to be made. She then becomes an active member of M.A.C, and helps Sheila arrest the eponymous duo. However, she's horrified after witnessing the catastrophic results of her actions, and quits the group to find Stan before he gets hurt. Awful Wedded Life: By Season 23, it's become clear she no longer even likes Randy. As soon as he gets arrested, she takes down all his pictures claiming it's because seeing him reminds her that Randy went to prison.
